floor.why: release-proof.yml:219-320 records the defect these two numbers exist to refuse, live in this repository: 'pytest exits 0 when every test skips'. A cluster lane whose container failed to start runs 186 skips and reports success. min_executed may RISE and max_skipped may FALL as the suite is repaired; moving either one the other way to obtain a green is the single most damaging edit available in this file.

policy.the_exit_status_is_pytests: The lane runs pytest, captures its exit status, and hands it to the report with --pytest-rc. A non-zero value is final: the report exits with it regardless of how every node id classifies. It also refuses a run whose JUnit XML records failures while the caller claims pytest exited 0, which is the one rewiring that would let a fully-inventoried red run present as green.
policy.what_this_file_may_never_become: A place to put a test that started failing. Every entry below names a defect that existed before this lane did, is owned by a named lead, and is expected to be DELETED from here rather than to live here. A new failure is reported NEW.
policy.the_NEW_of_2026_08_14_were_deliberately_: The 2026-08-14 re-measurement reported 3 NEW: test_transitions.py's test_materialise_checks_issues_a_receipt_and_moves_the_subject, test_merge_with_an_open_obligation_is_a_refused_envelope and test_sign_disposition_then_merge_commits, each erroring in SETUP with `psycopg.errors.SerializationFailure: restart transaction: TransactionRetryWithProtoRefreshError: TransactionRetryError: retry txn (RETRY_SERIALIZABLE - failed preemptive refresh)`. They are NOT recorded in `groups`, and the omission is the point: adding them is precisely the edit the rule above forbids, and it would take three tests off their owner's screen on the day they first appeared. They stay NEW until the lead who owns test_transitions.py rules on them. TWO THINGS ABOUT THEM ARE WORTH THE NEXT READER'S TIME. First, 40001 RETRY_SERIALIZABLE is the error class the platform brief says a single-node local CockroachDB 'never triggers' and that CockroachDB Cloud will require a retry loop for - it has now been triggered locally, so the brief's premise is measurably weaker than it reads, and the retry loop is not a Cloud-only concern. Second, all three are in test_transitions.py, the same module as all three `unstable` entries, which is where this file already records measured cross-test contamination.
policy.unstable_is_not_a_loophole: `unstable` entries are exempt from the CEILING check and from nothing else - they still fail pytest, and pytest still fails the lane. Each carries the number of runs it was observed over and the number in which it failed; the schema refuses an entry without them, and refuses one that failed every run it was seen in. An unstable entry that PASSES is reported as a notice, not silently, so that a genuine fix to the contamination is still visible to whoever made it.

groups.cause: KeyError: "'commit_v2' is not an identifier the deployed demo seed produces", raised in the `payloads` fixture during SETUP, which is why these are errors and not failures. The fixture is deliberate and its own message says so: the database is built by applying the two seed files scripts/deploy/seed_demo.py applies to CockroachDB Cloud, so a name that is absent is a ROW THE DEPLOYED DEMO DOES NOT CARRY. Resolving this by minting the row in the fixture is the edit this repository has already caught once and reverted. The fixture names the subjects it CAN offer, and as of 2026-08-14 that list is: check_id, clause_gen, clause_uuid, commit_id, countersigner_credential_id, countersigner_sub, cr_external_ref, cr_id, cr_state, cr_target_ref, doc_id, event_id, permit_external_ref, permit_id, permit_state, policy_version, receipt_id, run_id, signer_credential_id, signer_sub, silence_receipt_id, site_code, site_id, site_role. `commit_v2` is absent from it; `cr_id` is present, which is the evidence that the superseded cause below was genuinely resolved rather than merely re-worded.

cause_superseded.superseded_by: W5 (lane-controls wave), against a JUnit XML it produced itself; see measured.re_measured
cause_superseded.why_it_moved: An earlier worker seeded a change-request row, so `cr_id` became resolvable and the fixture walked on to the NEXT subject the seed does not carry. The 63 node ids did not move: the `payloads` fixture is session-scoped and builds all twelve read resources before any test runs, so one missing subject errors the whole group and fixing it only reveals the next one. That is why the membership of this group is stable while its cause is not, and it is why a `cause` field has to be re-measured rather than assumed.
cause_superseded.why_editing_this_field_is_not_the_forbid: A `cause` is a DESCRIPTION OF AN OBSERVATION. Nothing is checked against it - scripts/ci/cluster_lane_report.py requires only that it be non-empty, precisely so that a node id cannot be filed here without a reason. It is not a floor, a ceiling, a fixture, a seed or an expected value, so correcting it against a fresh measurement does not move an authoritative side to match a derived one; leaving it stale, on the other hand, certifies the wrong defect. The superseded text is preserved here rather than overwritten, per this file's own convention for superseded numbers.

ceiling_fired.what_was_measured: This node id PASSED. scripts/ci/cluster_lane_report.py reported it as `FIXED` and raised its CEILING verdict by name: '1 known-red test(s) now PASS ... Remove them from qa/cluster-known-red.json in the commit that fixed them.'
ceiling_fired.why_it_was_NOT_deleted_here: The CEILING is the one direction this file may move, and it may move only in the commit that FIXES the entry. W5 did not fix it - another lead's uncommitted work in this shared tree did. Deleting it here would detach the ceiling from the change that earned it, hand the list a second owner, and leave the fixing commit with nothing to show. The lane-controls plan rules this explicitly (R5.iii): 'Entries leave it only in the commit that FIXES them.' So the entry STAYS, the lane STAYS red on this verdict, and the verdict keeps naming the id until its owner deletes it. A ceiling nobody is made to lower is a ceiling that never falls - and a ceiling lowered by somebody who did not do the work is a ceiling that fell for free.
